lessons.title: Have to for Responsibilities
lessons.content: 'Have to' is used for responsibilities at work and in everyday life. It is conjugated as a regular verb and requires an auxiliary verb in questions and negatives. The structure is Subject + have to + V1.

details.explanation: 'Have to' is used for work-related responsibilities.
details.example: I have to write a letter to John.
details.burmese: ကျွန်တော် ဂျွန်ဆီ စာတစ်စောင် ရေးစရာရှိတယ်။

details.explanation: 'Have to' is used when something prevents you from doing something else.
details.example: Mike can't come because he has to work tomorrow.
details.burmese: မိုက် အလပ်လပ်စရာရှိလို့ သူ မလာနိုင်ဘူး။

details.explanation: 'Have to' is used for educational requirements.
details.example: Children have to go to school.

details.explanation: 'Have to' is used for health-related obligations.
details.example: He has to see the doctor.
details.burmese: သူ ဆရာဝန်ဆီ သွားရမယ်။

lessons.title: Don't Have to for Not Required
lessons.content: 'Don't have to' is used to express that something is not required or not necessary. The structure is Subject + don't/doesn't have to + V1.

details.explanation: 'Don't have to' means something is not necessary.
details.example: I don't have to work on Sundays so I can do what I want.
details.burmese: ကျွန်တော် တနင်္ဂနွေနေ့တွေ အလပ်မရဘူး။ ဒါကြောင့် ငါ ဘာလုပ်ချင်တာလုပ်နိုင်တယ်။

details.explanation: 'Don't have to' means attendance is optional.
details.example: She doesn't have to come to the meeting if she doesn't want to.
details.burmese: အစည်းအဝေး မလာချင်ရင် မလာပါနဲ့။

details.explanation: 'Don't have to' means driving is not necessary.
details.example: You don't have to drive today.
details.burmese: မင်း ဒီနေ့ မောင်းစရာ မလိုဘူး။

details.explanation: 'Don't have to' means learning a language is not necessary.
details.example: She doesn't have to learn your language.
details.burmese: သူမ မင်းဘာသာစကား သင်စရာ မလိုဘူး။

lessons.title: Have to in Past, Present, and Future
lessons.content: 'Have to' is used in all three tenses. The past form is 'had to'. Questions in the past use 'Did + subject + have to'.

details.explanation: Use 'have to' or 'has to' for present obligations.
details.example: I have to file reports every week.
details.burmese: ငါ အပတ်တိုင်း အစီရင်ခံစာ တင်ရမယ်။

details.example: She had to pick the children up from school yesterday.
details.burmese: သူမ မနေ့က ကလေးတွေကို ကျောင်းကနေ ခေါ်လာခရတယ်။

details.explanation: Use 'Did + subject + have to' for past questions.
details.example: Did he have to leave so early?
details.burmese: သူ အစောစောထွက်လိုက်ရတာလား။

details.explanation: 'Had to' is used for past obligations like doctor visits.
details.example: I had to go to the dentist yesterday.
details.burmese: ငါ မနေ့က သွားဆရာဝန်ဆီ သွားရတယ်။

details.explanation: 'Did + have to' is used to ask about past work obligations.
details.example: Did they have to do the work over again?
details.burmese: သူတို့ အလုပ်ကို ပြန်လုပ်ရတာလား။
